title: Maximum Profit With Job Scheduling
description: We have `n` jobs, where each job `i` has a `startTime[i]`, `endTime[i]`, and `profit[i]`. Find the maximum profit you can take such that no two jobs in the subset overlap.
input_format: First line contains `n`. Second line contains `startTime`. Third line contains `endTime`. Fourth line contains `profit`.
hints: Sort jobs by their end times.
Use dynamic programming with binary search: `dp[i]` stores `(end_time, max_profit)`.
For each job, binary search the latest non-overlapping job to take `dp[prev] + profit`.

reference_solution:
import sys, bisect
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    starts = [int(x) for x in data[1:1+n]]
    ends = [int(x) for x in data[1+n:1+2*n]]
    profits = [int(x) for x in data[1+2*n:1+3*n]]
    jobs = sorted(zip(starts, ends, profits), key=lambda x: x[1])
    dp = [(0, 0)]
    for s, e, p in jobs:
        idx = bisect.bisect_right(dp, (s, float('inf'))) - 1
        cur_profit = dp[idx][1] + p
        if cur_profit > dp[-1][1]:
            dp.append((e, cur_profit))
    print(dp[-1][1])
